data.narrative:
Fulfil is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mir Aamir that has raised $127M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable firms—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private—operating in the same sector and stage. Key private comparables include Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $127M capital raised as a proxy base, yielding $241M. Peer-median analysis identifies three same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.6B to $2.0B—Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Generalist AI at $2.0B—producing a median of $1.75B. The wide dispersion between methods reflects heterogeneity in growth trajectories and stage interpretation within the peer set.

The triangulated range is $205M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $996M. The stage-progression method yields materially lower results, suggesting either that Fulfil's raised capital trails peer growth rates or that comparables command a sector premium. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage-to-stage multiplier for this robotics subsector, revenue traction relative to peers, and whether the public comparable commands a public-market discount. A central valuation of approximately $1.0B–$1.2B may be most defensible pending revenue disclosure.
